title: Read state with a selector
summary: A selector is a function that chooses a useful part of state.
introduction: A selector is a function that chooses a useful part of state. Your task: Create a selector that doubles the reading count.
learningObjectives: Create a selector that doubles the reading count.
Explain the example for read state with a selector

blocks.text: A selector is a function that chooses a useful part of state. createSelector can remember its last input and result.

Use an Angular project with the matching major version of @ngrx/store. Effects and SignalStore examples also need @ngrx/effects or @ngrx/signals. Save linked snippets in the files named by their imports.

items: `createSelector` combines state readers into a reusable derived result and can reuse the last calculation.

blocks.text: The selector returns 4 from the reading slice.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Selectors should read and calculate. Do not change state or send actions inside them.
